Multiobjective Scheduling in Distributed
Heterogeneous Flexible Job Shops
Lijun Wang , Chengguang Wang , Xiangyang Li , Ruixue Cheng , Xiao Ma, and Dong Liu
Abstract—To address the issues of insufficient population
diversity and the tendency to fall into local convergence in
the NSGA-II algorithm for distributed heterogeneous flexible
job shop scheduling, a dual-population improved algorithm,
D3QN-NSGA-II, based on D3QN is proposed. By introducing
a dual-population evolution strategy, the breeding population
and the regular population are divided using a reproductive
capacity assessment mechanism, with differentiated crossover
and mutation operators designed for each. A hybrid strategy,
consisting of 12 types of local search operators across 3 categories,
is constructed, and the innovative application of D3QN deep rein-
forcement learning for dynamic operator selection is introduced.
Additionally, an energy-efficient scheduling strategy is applied
to optimize machine idle time. Finally, the effectiveness of the
D3QN-NSGA-II algorithm is evaluated using 20 instances, with
experimental results demonstrating its superiority over several
other advanced algorithms in solving the DHFJS problem.
Index Terms—Distributed manufacturing, D3QN, metaheuris-
tic algorithms, modeling simulation, optimal scheduling.

decision-making abilities of reinforcement learning. It employs
environmental data as input to obtain experiences of success or
failure, which are then utilized to update the parameters of the
decision network, thereby facilitating optimal decision-making

ing the algorithm’s overall performance and stability. In light of
the considerable state space inherent to DHFJS, the deployment
of D3QN proves instrumental in enabling the learning and
selection of optimal operators.
In consideration of the existing research, this article proposes
the D3QN-based dual-population NSGA-II (D3QN-NSGA-II)
algorithm as a potential solution to the energy-efficient schedul-

tify the solution that minimizes both the maximum completion
time and total energy consumption. Compared with existing
studies, the main contributions of this algorithm are: 1) de-
signing a two-population evolutionary strategy to enhance the
global and local optimization capabilities by differentially as-
signing search targets through a reproductive capacity evalu-
ation mechanism; 2) constructing an operator dynamic selec-
tion framework that incorporates deep reinforcement learning,
and adaptively matching the optimal strategy from 12 loca
search operators by using D3QN; and 3) introducing an energy-
efficient scheduling strategy to achieve energy-efficiency and
energy-saving optimization by optimizing the machine idle time
to achieve the synergistic optimization of energy efficiency and
efficiency. The superiority of the D3QN-NSGA-II in solving
the multiobjective heterogeneous flexible job shop scheduling
problem is validated through simulation experiments on case
studies, which demonstrate its capacity to obtain superior Pareto
solutions.

tion II formulates the DHFJS problem, defines relevant sym-

Section III details the proposed D3QN-NSGA-II algorithm,
including encoding strategies, dual-population evolution, local
search operators, energy-saving strategies, and D3QN-based
operator selection. Section IV describes the experimental setup,
parameter validation, component separation experiments, and
comparative results. Finally, Section V concludes the article and
outlines future research directions.

D. Energy Saving Strategy
In the context of scheduling problems with consideration of
energy consumption, the total energy consumption is a criti-
cal metric that significantly impacts the achievement of green
scheduling. One principal method for reducing energy con-
sumption during the production of jobs is to minimize both
machine processing time and idle time. In accordance with this
principle, an energy-saving strategy has been devised which
places an emphasis on local optimization and the modification
of production sequences with a view to reducing idle time on
machines and, consequently, lowering overall energy consump-
tion throughout the production process.
The strategy is based on the following principles: 1) local
optimization: the application of local search techniques is uti-
lized for the optimization of operational sequencing on machin-
ery, with the objective of minimizing downtime and enhancing
machine utilization; 2) adjusting production sequences: the re-
ordering of operations or the adjustment of their start times may
be employed to more effectively utilize machine capacity and
reduce periods of inactivity; and 3) reduction of idle time: the
objective is to identify and reduce instances of idle time between
operations, thereby reducing unnecessary energy consumption.

The Q-value, represented by
Q ( s , a )
, is an implicit indication
of the value associated with being in state s and the advantage
gained from selecting action a. In response to this, the Dueling
network [20] was developed with the explicit objective of segre-
gating the state value and action advantage components within
a given state. In the context of the dueling network framework,
two distinct networks are employed with the objective of esti-
mating the state value function,
V ( s )
, and the action advantage
function,
A ( s , a )
, for each state. Subsequently, the action value
function
Q ( s , \ a )
is derived by integrating the aforementioned
networks, as illustrated in the following equation:

\begin{array}{l} Q (s, a; \theta , \alpha , \beta) = V (s; \theta , \beta) \\ \qquad + \left(A (s, a; \theta , \alpha) - \frac {1}{| A |} \sum_ {a ^ {\prime}} A (s, a ^ {\prime}; \theta , \alpha)\right). \end{array}\tag{21}
Fig. 4 illustrates the network architecture of the D3QN, de-
picting how the state inputs are processed through the hidden
layers to generate action values, highlighting the separation
of state value and action advantage branches in the dueling
network design. The D3QN network consists of an input layer,
three fully connected layers (with 64, 128, and 64 neurons, re-
spectively, all using the ReLU activation function), a branching
fully connected layer (split into the value stream and advantage
stream), and an output layer.

The efficacy of an algorithm is significantly influenced by
its key parameters. Prior to conducting simulation experiments,
it is of paramount importance to validate and optimize the
parameters for both the proposed algorithm and the selected
comparative algorithms. To ensure fairness and consistency in
the comparison, all algorithms (including MOEA/D, MOPSO,
NSWOA, and MOGWO) adopt the same Taguchi method for
parameter tuning, which is used to assess the impact of var-
ious parameters on algorithm performance and obtain opti-
mal parameter combinations. The experiments are conducted
based on the 20J3F test case, where each parameter combi-
nation is independently run ten times, and the results of the
parameter validation are presented in Table II. For compar-
ative algorithms, parameters were not directly adopted from
original literature but retuned specifically for the DHFJS prob-
lem in this study, following the same Taguchi method frame-
work as D3QN-NSGA-II to ensure comparable experimental
conditions.

posed strategy, we designed a comparative experiment to eval-
uate the effects of the dual-population evolutionary strategy,
energy-efficient scheduling strategy, and D3QN-based operator

ment compared the basic NSGA-II algorithm, NSGA-II with
only the dual-population evolutionary strategy (DP+NSGA-
II), NSGA-II with only the energy-efficient scheduling strat-
egy (ES+NSGA-II), NSGA-II with only the D3QN-based
operator selection mechanism (D3QN+NSGA-II), and the
complete algorithm (D3QN-NSGA-II). To ensure the relia-
bility of the experimental results, identical parameter set-
tings were used for all the algorithms, and each variant was
run ten times across 20 test cases to compute the average
performance.

V. CONCLUSION
The D3QN-NSGA-II algorithm incorporates the attributes of
deep reinforcement learning and multiobjective optimization.
By employing a dual-population strategy and a D3QN-based
operator selection mechanism, the algorithm effectively bal-
ances global exploration and local exploitation, thereby enhanc-
ing both the convergence speed and the quality of solutions.
A detailed description and modeling of the DHFJS problem
have led to the definition of rational objective functions and
constraints, thereby providing a clear framework for algorithm
design and application. Comparative experiments with existing
algorithms have consistently demonstrated that D3QN-NSGA-
II exhibits superior performance across a range of test cases,
as evidenced by metrics such as HV and IGD. These findings
validate the effectiveness and superiority of D3QN-NSGA-II.
From a management practice perspective, this study pro-
vides a scheduling method for the manufacturing industry that
optimizes both efficiency and energy consumption. The dual-
population evolutionary strategy guides companies in dynami-
cally allocating search resources during production scheduling,
improving global optimization capabilities. The D3QN-based
operator selection mechanism helps adaptively adjust schedul-
ing strategies based on real-time production states, enhancing
the algorithm’s adaptability to complex production scenarios.
The energy-saving scheduling strategy offers a feasible path
to reduce machine idle energy consumption and optimize re-
source utilization, providing practical guidance for companies
in achieving green manufacturing and cost control.
Future research could explore the incorporation of additional
optimization objectives (such as cost and quality) and improve
the algorithms robustness against uncertainties like machine
failures and demand fluctuations.
